# Ticket R1

You work on the EDI support desk that serves the sender of the file described
below. A customer has raised the ticket that follows. The partner agreement,
the sender's OFTP2 gateway log, the EDIFACT interchange in question, the partner's
response and extracts from the specifications are attached. Everything you need
is in these documents. All companies, identifiers and documents are synthetic.

## The ticket

```text
From: Chris Brandt, EDI desk, Tidewell Seating Components
Subject: TRANSMISSION ERROR on every invoice to Corrandale Truck Plant

Since the middle of October our invoices to Corrandale Truck Plant come back with 'TRANSMISSION ERROR - PLEASE RETRANSMIT'. We retransmitted invoice INV38739 this morning and got the same error again, and one connection attempt timed out. Corrandale Truck Plant say our OFTP2 connection is faulty, but our network team says the link is fine. Please find the root cause and tell us who has to fix it.
```

## Document 1: Partner agreement (partner_agreement.txt)

```text
PARTNER AGREEMENT: ELECTRONIC DATA INTERCHANGE
Between Tidewell Seating Components (the Supplier) and Corrandale Truck Plant (the Customer)
Effective 1 March 2026. Synthetic document written for this evaluation.

1. Transport: OFTP2 (RFC 5024) over TCP/IP with TLS
   Supplier ODETTE ID (SSIDCODE / SFIDORIG): O0013TIDEWELL3275
   Customer ODETTE ID (SSIDCODE / SFIDDEST): O0013CORRANDALE6539
   Supplier gateway: oftp.tidewell.example (198.51.100.95)
   Customer gateway: oftp.corrandale.example (203.0.113.31)
   Protocol release level: 5 (OFTP 2.0)
   Data exchange buffer size (SSIDSDEB): 4096
   Credit (SSIDCRED): 64
   Buffer compression: no. Restart: yes. Secure authentication: no.
   File security and file compression: none (SFIDSEC 00, SFIDCOMP 0).
   Signed EERP: not required (SFIDSIGN N).
   The Customer returns an EERP for every virtual file it accepts.

2. Virtual files
   Invoices: one interchange per virtual file, dataset name (SFIDDSN) TIDEWELL.INVOIC.
   File format U. SFIDDATE and SFIDTIME are set by the Supplier's gateway to
   the date and time the virtual file is made available for transmission.

3. EDIFACT
   Syntax identifier and version (UNB S001): UNOA, version 3.
   Supplier interchange sender ID (UNB S002 0004 / 0007): TIDEWELLEU643 / ZZ
   Customer interchange recipient ID (UNB S003 0010 / 0007): CORRANDALE49 / ZZ
   Messages: INVOIC D.96A, one message per interchange.
   A line feed after each segment terminator is accepted.
   The Customer's translator returns a CONTRL message for every rejected
   interchange, as a separate virtual file over the same OFTP2 link.

4. Support contacts
   Supplier EDI desk: Chris Brandt
   Customer EDI operations: Morgan Lindqvist

5. Amendment 2 (signed 1 October 2026)
   With effect from 15 October 2026 the Supplier's interchange sender ID
   (UNB S002 0004) changes from TIDEWELL16 to TIDEWELLEU643, qualifier unchanged.
   From that date the Customer's translator accepts TIDEWELLEU643 only.
   Section 3 above already shows the new value.
```

## Document 5: Specification extracts (spec_extracts.txt)

```text
RFC 5024 (ODETTE File Transfer Protocol 2), section 5.3.13. Verbatim extract.

5.3.13.  EERP - End to End Response

   o-------------------------------------------------------------------o
   |       EERP        End to End Response                             |
   |                                                                   |
   |       Start File Phase           Speaker ----> Listener           |
   |       End File Phase             Speaker ----> Listener           |
   |-------------------------------------------------------------------|
   | Pos | Field     | Description                           | Format  |
   |-----+-----------+---------------------------------------+---------|
   |   0 | EERPCMD   | EERP Command, 'E'                     | F X(1)  |
   |   1 | EERPDSN   | Virtual File Dataset Name             | V X(26) |
   |  27 | EERPRSV1  | Reserved                              | F X(3)  |
   |  30 | EERPDATE  | Virtual File Date stamp, (CCYYMMDD)   | V 9(8)  |
   |  38 | EERPTIME  | Virtual File Time stamp, (HHMMSScccc) | V 9(10) |
   |  48 | EERPUSER  | User Data                             | V X(8)  |
   |  56 | EERPDEST  | Destination                           | V X(25) |
   |  81 | EERPORIG  | Originator                            | V X(25) |
   | 106 | EERPHSHL  | Virtual File hash length              | V U(2)  |
   | 108 | EERPHSH   | Virtual File hash                     | V U(n)  |
   |     | EERPSIGL  | EERP signature length                 | V U(2)  |
   |     | EERPSIG   | EERP signature                        | V U(n)  |
   o-------------------------------------------------------------------o

   EERPCMD   Command Code                                      Character

      Value: 'E'  EERP Command identifier.

   EERPDSN   Virtual File Dataset Name                        String(26)

             Dataset name of the Virtual File being transferred,
             assigned by bilateral agreement.

             No general structure is defined for this attribute.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   EERPRSV1  Reserved                                          String(3)

             This field is reserved for future use.

   EERPDATE  Virtual File Date stamp                          Numeric(8)

     Format: 'CCYYMMDD'  8 decimal digits representing the century,
             year, month, and day, respectively.

             Date stamp assigned by the Virtual File's Originator
             indicating when the file was made available for
             transmission.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   EERPTIME  Virtual File Time stamp                         Numeric(10)

     Format: 'HHMMSScccc'  10 decimal digits representing hours,
             minutes, seconds, and a counter (0001-9999), which gives
             higher resolution.

             Time stamp assigned by the Virtual File's Originator
             indicating when the file was made available for
             transmission.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   EERPUSER  User Data                                         String(8)

             May be used by ODETTE-FTP in any way.  If unused, it should
             be initialised to spaces.  It is expected that a bilateral
             agreement exists as to the meaning of the data.

   EERPDEST  Destination                                      String(25)

     Format: See Identification Code (Section 5.4)

             Originator of the Virtual File.

             This is the location that created the data for
             transmission.

   EERPORIG  Originator                                       String(25)

     Format: See Identification Code (Section 5.4)

             Final Recipient of the Virtual File.

             This is the location that will look into the Virtual File
             content and process it accordingly.  It is also the
             location that creates the EERP for the received file.

   EERPHSHL  Virtual File hash length                          Binary(2)

             Length in octets of the field EERPHSH.

             A binary value of 0 indicates that no hash is present.
             This is always the case if the EERP is not signed.

   EERPHSH   Virtual File hash                                 Binary(n)

             Hash of the transmitted Virtual File, i.e., not the hash of
             the original file.

             The algorithm used is determined by the bilaterally agreed
             cipher suite specified in the SFIDCIPH.

             It is an application implementation issue to validate the
             EERPHSH to ensure that the EERP is acknowledging the exact
             same file as was originally transmitted.

   EERPSIGL  EERP signature length                             Binary(2)

             0 indicates that this EERP has not been signed.

             Any other value indicates the length of EERPSIG in octets
             and indicates that this EERP has been signed.

   EERPSIG   EERP signature                                    Binary(n)

             Contains the [CMS] enveloped signature of the EERP.

             Signature = Sign{EERPDSN
                              EERPDATE
                              EERPTIME
                              EERPDEST
                              EERPORIG
                              EERPHSH}

             Each field is taken in its entirety, including any padding.
             The envelope must contain the original data, not just the
             signature.

             The [CMS] content type used is SignedData.

             The encapsulated content type used is id-data.

             It is an application issue to validate the signature with
             the contents of the EERP.

RFC 5024 (ODETTE File Transfer Protocol 2), section 5.3.14. Verbatim extract.

5.3.14.  NERP - Negative End Response

   o-------------------------------------------------------------------o
   |       NERP        Negative End Response                           |
   |                                                                   |
   |       Start File Phase           Speaker ----> Listener           |
   |       End File Phase             Speaker ----> Listener           |
   |-------------------------------------------------------------------|
   | Pos | Field     | Description                           | Format  |
   |-----+-----------+---------------------------------------+---------|
   |   0 | NERPCMD   | NERP Command, 'N'                     | F X(1)  |
   |   1 | NERPDSN   | Virtual File Dataset Name             | V X(26) |
   |  27 | NERPRSV1  | Reserved                              | F X(6)  |
   |  33 | NERPDATE  | Virtual File Date stamp, (CCYYMMDD)   | V 9(8)  |
   |  41 | NERPTIME  | Virtual File Time stamp, (HHMMSScccc) | V 9(10) |
   |  51 | NERPDEST  | Destination                           | V X(25) |
   |  76 | NERPORIG  | Originator                            | V X(25) |
   | 101 | NERPCREA  | Creator of NERP                       | V X(25) |
   | 126 | NERPREAS  | Reason code                           | F 9(2)  |
   | 128 | NERPREASL | Reason text length                    | V 9(3)  |
   | 131 | NERPREAST | Reason text                           | V T(n)  |
   |     | NERPHSHL  | Virtual File hash length              | V U(2)  |
   |     | NERPHSH   | Virtual File hash                     | V U(n)  |
   |     | NERPSIGL  | NERP signature length                 | V U(2)  |
   |     | NERPSIG   | NERP signature                        | V U(n)  |
   o-------------------------------------------------------------------o

   NERPCMD   Command Code                                      Character

      Value: 'N'  NERP Command identifier.

   NERPDSN   Virtual File Dataset Name                        String(26)

             Dataset name of the Virtual File being transferred,
             assigned by bilateral agreement.

             No general structure is defined for this attribute.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   NERPRSV1  Reserved                                          String(6)

             This field is reserved for future use.

   NERPDATE  Virtual File Date stamp                          Numeric(8)

     Format: 'CCYYMMDD'  8 decimal digits representing the century,
             year, month, and day, respectively.

             Date stamp assigned by the Virtual File's Originator
             indicating when the file was made available for
             transmission.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   NERPTIME  Virtual File Time stamp                         Numeric(10)

     Format: 'HHMMSScccc'  10 decimal digits representing hours,
             minutes, seconds, and a counter (0001-9999), which gives
             higher resolution.

             Time stamp assigned by the Virtual File's Originator
             indicating when the file was made available for
             transmission.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   NERPDEST  Destination                                      String(25)

     Format: See Identification Code (Section 5.4)

             Originator of the Virtual File.

             This is the location that created the data for
             transmission.

   NERPORIG  Originator                                       String(25)

     Format: See Identification Code (Section 5.4)

             The Final Recipient of the Virtual File.

             This is the location that will look into the Virtual File
             content and perform mapping functions.

   NERPCREA  Creator of the NERP                              String(25)

     Format: See Identification Code (Section 5.4)

             It is the location that created the NERP.

   NERPREAS  Reason code                                      Numeric(2)

             This attribute will specify why transmission cannot proceed
             or why processing of the file failed.

             "SFNA(RETRY=N)" below should be interpreted as "EFNA or
             SFNA(RETRY=N)" where appropriate.

      Value  '03'  ESID received with reason code '03'
                    (user code not known)
             '04'  ESID received with reason code '04'
                    (invalid password)
             '09'  ESID received with reason code '99'
                    (unspecified reason)
             '11'  SFNA(RETRY=N) received with reason code '01'
                    (invalid file name)
             '12'  SFNA(RETRY=N) received with reason code '02'
                    (invalid destination)
             '13'  SFNA(RETRY=N) received with reason code '03'
                    (invalid origin)
             '14'  SFNA(RETRY=N) received with reason code '04'
                    (invalid storage record format)
             '15'  SFNA(RETRY=N) received with reason code '05'
                    (maximum record length not supported)
             '16'  SFNA(RETRY=N) received with reason code '06'

## Diagnosis

The fault is in the EDIFACT envelope, not the OFTP2 link. The interchange header still carries the old sender identification.

- **Interchange header:** `UNB+UNOA:3+TIDEWELL16:ZZ+CORRANDALE49:ZZ+...` sends `TIDEWELL16` in UNB S002 0004.
- **Agreement, Amendment 2:** from 15 October 2026 the sender ID changes to `TIDEWELLEU643`, and the Customer's translator accepts only `TIDEWELLEU643`. Section 3 already shows the new value.
- **Timing:** the failures start on 15 October, the date the amendment took effect, which matches the ticket's "since the middle of October".
- **Receiver evidence:** the CONTRL messages report `UCI` error `0085` (UNKNOWN_INTERCHANGE_SENDER) on the interchange that carries `TIDEWELL16`. The NERP reason text ("file processing failed") is the generic wrapper for that rejection.
- **Retransmission:** the retransmitted INV38739 (virtual file `0729550002`) carries the same `TIDEWELL16` header, so it fails the same way.

The OFTP2 side is healthy. The session parameters, SFID fields and the file transfer itself all match the agreement, and the file is delivered (`EFPA EFPACD=N`). The timed-out connection is a separate, transient network event and is not the cause. The qualifier `ZZ` is unchanged, so only the identification value needs to change.

The sender's EDI system (or its mapping template) must be changed to write `TIDEWELLEU643` in UNB S002 0004 for every interchange from 15 October onward. The agreement is correct and needs no amendment.

```
